resources.string: Use Table for a device left on a surface, Pocket for your pocket, Bag for a bag or backpack, and Journey for a time-limited Pocket or Bag session.
Phone Guard combines the sensors actually available on the device and will not claim a mode is supported when the detector cannot reach a reliable alarm decision.
Set a 4–6 digit PIN and optionally enable strong biometrics. Unlocking the phone alone does not authenticate Phone Guard.
Detection runs locally. Siren, vibration, flash and the warning screen are best-effort outputs subject to Android and OEM limits.

Table monitors calibrated motion. Pocket and Bag use available proximity, light, motion and rotation evidence. Journey runs a time-limited Pocket or Bag session. Phone Guard only marks a mode available when its required sensor evidence is present.
Detection is processed on-device. Phone Guard does not record audio, use location, or capture photos or video. Event history stays in local app storage.
Camera permission is used only for Android torch/flash APIs. Phone Guard never uses the camera to capture images or video.
Phone Guard requires no registration or login. Core protection works locally without a proprietary account or backend.
Non-sensitive preferences may use Android backup or device transfer. PIN verifier data, active protection state, alarm-volume lease and event history are excluded.

When you arm protection, one visible foreground service monitors the selected sensors. The service stops when protection is disarmed. Android or the device manufacturer can still restrict background execution in exceptional cases.

Siren, vibration, flash, alarm volume and visual warning are best-effort outputs. Do Not Disturb, OEM policy, unavailable hardware, force-stop or system shutdown can limit them. The app reports effective capability instead of guaranteeing an override.
Phone Guard is a local deterrence and alert tool. It cannot physically prevent theft, power-off, force-stop or operating-system actions.
